title: 2005 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 4
statement: Prove that an \(m \times n\) rectangle is \((b, b)\)-tileable if and only if \(2 b \mid m\) and \(2 b \mid n\).

solutions.text: Color the first \(b\) rows of an \(m \times n\) rectangle black, the next \(b\) white, the next \(b\) black, etc. Any \((b, b)\) domino covers one square of each color, so for the rectangle to be \((b, b)\)-tileable, there must be the same number of black squares as white squares. This is possible only when \(2 b \mid m\). Similarly, we must have \(2 b \mid n\). It is easy to exhibit a tiling of all such rectangles, proving the claim. (It is also possible to prove this using the lemma described below.)
